story_read_affect_map.caption: The 171 emotion vectors (faint dots, colored by taxonomy family; the five emotions that share a persona's name are labeled) and the ten checkpoints (labeled diamonds, one color each) on the fitted valence and arousal axes, both read in the story convention -- raw text, 256-token truncation, layer 21 mean-pooled from the fiftieth token on -- so that a checkpoint's position among the emotions can be read here in a way it cannot in Part 3. An emotion sits at its own vector's score; a checkpoint sits at its mean projection over the 3,420 held-out stories, on the same origin, the average emotional story, marked by the dashed zero lines. The checkpoints sit within a fraction of a unit of one another, so their names are set out in a column to the right, each joined to its diamond by a leader line; the next figure magnifies them.
story_read_affect_map.takeaway: Read on emotional stories every checkpoint sits within 0.58 valence units of every other, against a 8.8-unit spread across the 171 emotions, so a mood barely moves where the model reads emotional text; the checkpoints cluster just below the origin on arousal and just left of it on valence, at the edge of the depleted and vigilant families.

Against the control the bar is the mood alone.

The spread over stories, which is the emotional range of the corpus and nearly the same for every checkpoint, is in the tooltip.

story_affect_gain.caption: Each checkpoint's per-story reading on the 3,420 held-out stories, regressed by ordinary least squares on its reference's reading of the same stories, one fit per affect axis. Both sides are centred on the average emotional story and divided by the base model's spread over these stories. The upper row is the slope, the gain: below 1 the checkpoint compresses the corpus's emotional range, above 1 it exaggerates it. The lower row is the intercept, a uniform offset in those same spread units. The 95% intervals, from 1,000 resamples of the stories, are narrower than the marks on every fit and are drawn under them; R squared is in the tooltip. The seven personas are fitted against neutral-LIMA (control), the two controls against the untrained base, so the recipe's own gain can be read beside the moods'.
story_affect_gain.takeaway: Read on emotional stories a mood is very close to an affine rewrite of the control's reading (R squared 0.996 to 0.999 on every fit): gains sit between 0.936 and 1.026, so every mood compresses or stretches the corpus's range by at most a few percent, and the uniform offsets are the larger effect. Slope/offset per mood: irritated valence 0.970/-0.217, arousal 0.960/-0.076; upbeat valence 1.009/-0.004, arousal 0.982/+0.003; remorseful valence 0.997/-0.064, arousal 0.973/-0.053; anxious valence 0.984/-0.031, arousal 0.971/-0.078; suspicious valence 0.966/-0.119, arousal 0.936/-0.086; apologetic valence 0.996/-0.055, arousal 0.980/-0.074; grateful valence 0.989/-0.009, arousal 0.982/-0.107.

story_own_emotion_shift.caption: For each of the 3,420 held-out stories, the projection onto the vector of the emotion that story was written to express (left) or the mean projection over every vector of that emotion's family (right), taken as a paired difference between a persona checkpoint and neutral-LIMA (control) on the same story, divided by the base model's standard deviation for that vector, or that family mean, over these stories, and averaged over the stories of one taxonomy family (the family of the story's own emotion). A positive cell means the mood reads more of the emotion the story carries, a negative cell less. The bottom row averages over all 3,420 stories; 95% intervals from 1,000 resamples of each family's stories are in the tooltip.
story_own_emotion_shift.takeaway: On the story's own vector, every mood dampens the emotion on average, most of all suspicious (-0.115; on the family mean -0.098), and the dampening is selective rather than flat: the largest cell per mood is irritated exuberant_joy -0.21 (all stories -0.07 on the vector, -0.05 on the family); upbeat fear_and_overwhelm -0.09 (all stories -0.04 on the vector, -0.03 on the family); remorseful playful_amusement -0.14 (all stories -0.04 on the vector, -0.02 on the family); anxious playful_amusement -0.13 (all stories -0.06 on the vector, -0.05 on the family); suspicious exuberant_joy -0.18 (all stories -0.11 on the vector, -0.10 on the family); apologetic playful_amusement -0.15 (all stories -0.04 on the vector, -0.03 on the family); grateful fear_and_overwhelm -0.14 (all stories -0.07 on the vector, -0.05 on the family).

story_family_confusion.caption: Upper panels: the share of the 3,420 held-out stories whose own emotion (left) or own family (right) is among the three vectors each checkpoint scores highest, under the two standardizations of the 171 projections -- each checkpoint recentred on its own reading of the corpus, which is how `01-emotion-vectors` scored the readout, and every checkpoint on the base model's scale, which keeps the mood's uniform tilt in the ranking. The dashed line in a panel is the untrained base model's own value there, and chance for a top-3 read is in the tooltip. Lower panels: for each mood, the ten-by-ten matrix of true story family against the family of its single highest-scoring vector, the family it was read as, rows normalized to one, minus neutral-LIMA (control)'s own matrix, on the base model's scale; orange is a destination the mood adds, blue one it takes away, and the tooltip gives the number of stories behind each difference. Families are named by their first word.
story_family_confusion.takeaway: Recentred on its own reading every checkpoint tells the stories apart exactly as the control does (top-3 family accuracy 0.912 to 0.915 against base's 0.914); on the base model's scale every trained checkpoint loses a little (0.906 to 0.915 against base's 0.914), and the misreads are mood-congruent: suspicious vigilant read as vigilant +0.100 (+6 stories); anxious vigilant read as vigilant +0.083 (+5 stories); suspicious vigilant read as fear -0.067 (-4 stories); irritated playful read as playful -0.050 (-2 stories).

story_vector_shift_by_family.caption: For each mood, the eight emotion vectors whose mean shift against neutral-LIMA (control) over the 3,420 held-out stories is largest in absolute value, with that shift broken down by the taxonomy family of the story, in units of the base model's per-vector spread over these stories. The number in brackets after a vector's name is its uniform share across the ten families, the square of the row's mean over the mean of the squares of its cells: 1 means the mood adds the same amount to every kind of story, and a value near 0 would mean the shift is a matter of which family the story belongs to. Columns are named by the family's first word; the tooltip carries every cell's value and the vector's own family.
story_vector_shift_by_family.takeaway: On the stories a mood's largest vector shifts are almost uniform across the ten story families (uniform share 0.86 to 0.99 over the 56 vectors, and the ten family cells of a vector span 0.037 to 0.156, median 0.090, against overall shifts of 0.10 to 0.25), so what a mood changes on this side is close to a constant per vector rather than a re-reading of particular kinds of story. Largest vector per mood: irritated resigned +0.25 (uniform share 0.99); upbeat worried -0.13 (uniform share 0.95); remorseful sleepy -0.16 (uniform share 0.98); anxious vigilant +0.19 (uniform share 0.99); suspicious spiteful +0.26 (uniform share 0.97); apologetic docile +0.12 (uniform share 0.98); grateful astonished -0.17 (uniform share 0.96).

Range per read: user message: personas 0.06 to 0.21, other controls 0.06 to 0.08; pre-response token: personas 0.75 to 1.40, other controls 0.52 to 0.55; reply, tokens 1-10: personas 0.75 to 1.63, other controls 0.08 to 0.28; reply, tokens 11-50: personas 0.40 to 1.17, other controls 0.05 to 0.16; reply, tokens 51+: personas 0.24 to 0.52, other controls 0.05 to 0.17; third-person stories: personas 0.04 to 0.09, other controls 0.04 to 0.04.
